h.select_rule: Discard hypotheses conditioning on the edited field's own value or making the edit inert. Keep 10 spanning at least five mechanism families, with at most two resting on redundancy or substitution, preferring those with a two-sided argument and a sharp refuting comparison.
h.strategy: Experts find three patterns obvious: conditioning on the edited field's own value, conditions that make the edit inert, and 'capacity is already supplied elsewhere, so the edit adds less'. At most two hypotheses may rest on that last redundancy argument. Draw the rest from distinct mechanism families. Optimization and gradient flow: an edit changes trainability depending on another part. Signal scale or variance: summing or merging streams changes magnitudes. Effective depth versus width. Regularization or overfitting: added capacity hurts when another part already fits easily. Complementarity: two different component types help more together than either predicts alone. Each hypothesis must couple two different fields, and no condition setting may appear more than twice. Write each 'why' in two parts: the mechanism and the outcome it predicts, then the strongest argument for the opposite direction and why you reject it.

hyps.why: Without the direct edge the output depends on routes through nodes 1 and 2, so low-pass pooling on edge 5 discards more needed information.
Pooled node 1 has lost high-frequency detail, so a conv on it gains less than on a conv or skip input.
A conv on edge 0 makes node 1 a learned feature, so a serial conv on edge 2 has more to build on.
Edge 0 only matters through its consumers, and a conv on edge 4 carries node 1's features to the output.
With no direct edge, the output relies on paths through node 2, so a conv on edge 5 carries more of the load.
With no direct edge, edge 4 is a main route to the output, so upgrading it to a conv matters more.
When the sibling edge into node 3 is parameter-free pooling, the direct conv is the main learned path, so its gain rises.
A skip on edge 0 gives edge 4 a clean input copy, whereas with edge 0 as none, edge 4 does nothing.
The identity bypass lets the network get by without the deep path, so a conv on edge 5 helps less.
An identity path from the input to node 3 already exists via edge 1, so a second identity adds little.
